name: Story checklist
description: Storytelling checks for any article, shown in the Writer's right column (OpenWriter, Story tab). Core items apply to every article. Optional techniques are the extras in the loop: go after one when it fits, never required. An outline can be picked per document; its sections tick off the same way. Items turn green when marked done. Later each item can get a scoring slot in prompts/; until then it is the writer's call. Sources: each technique cites the video and the 5-minute section where it is taught (t = seconds into the video).

items.label: Says one thing
items.question: What are you trying to say? One sentence, plain — if you can't say it simply, the piece isn't ready.

items.label: Believes it
items.question: Why do you believe what you're saying? The reason itself, not a citation.

items.label: Backed in your own words
items.question: What original thoughts or words back this up? Receipts point to sources; the spine of the argument has to be yours.

items.label: Great opening
items.question: Does the first paragraph make the reader need the next one?

items.label: Creates curiosity
items.question: Is there an open question the reader wants answered?

items.label: Holds information back
items.question: Is the answer withheld until it pays off, not given away early?

items.label: Drops you into a specific moment
items.question: Is there one concrete scene: a time, a place, a person? Not the helicopter view.

items.label: Creates tension
items.question: Is something uncertain and important at stake, that the reader wants resolved?

items.label: Explains enough
items.question: Is every idea as explained as it needs to be, no more (not lengthy, not too concise)?

items.label: Has its own personality
items.question: Does it sound like you, not like a summary?

items.label: Lands with a takeaway
items.question: Does the ending say what it meant, so the reader thinks: that's why you told me that?

items.label: Changes the pace
items.question: Slow down at the moments to experience; speed through what the reader only needs to know.

items.label: Starts somewhere unexpected
items.question: Does it open where nobody expected, so there is a reason to keep reading?

items.label: Leads, then twists
items.question: Is the reader led to a reasonable assumption, then shown something that makes them reinterpret it?

items.label: Just the right detail
items.question: Not lots of detail: the few specifics that let us see and feel it (Sunday afternoons, a sports bar, age 10 to 16).

items.label: A personal detail
items.question: One well-chosen personal detail shows the human behind the expertise. Personal, not private.

items.label: Leads with the main point
items.question: Is the point stated early, like a headline, so everything after it is easy to follow?

items.label: No skipped steps
items.question: Curse of knowledge: does it assume what the reader doesn't know? Jargon explained or gone?

items.label: Names the objection and answers it
items.question: Is the strongest resistance said in the reader's words, then answered? Naming it alone is not enough.

items.label: Data with a soul
items.question: Does a number come with what it means in someone's life, not just the figure?

items.label: Vivid sensory detail
items.question: Is the reader put in the room: what they would see and feel?

items.label: Logic, credibility and feeling
items.question: Logos and ethos are there; is pathos there too?

items.label: A less obvious answer
items.question: What would everyone else say here? Is there something they missed?

items.label: A third voice, not you vs them
items.question: Does a respected other (a mentor, a study, a witness) carry the challenge instead of your opinion?

items.label: Makes them feel it
items.question: Is the reader made to feel the idea, not only argued into it?

items.label: Reframes before the answer
items.question: Is the thing seen differently first (not a wheel: a time machine), before the new answer lands?

items.label: A sound bite
items.question: One short, sharp line that carries the whole idea?

items.label: Lets it land
items.question: Once the idea has landed, does it stop, instead of explaining it again?

items.label: Why it matters before how it works
items.question: Does it say why it matters before explaining the mechanism?

items.label: Simple words
items.question: Every term either explained (this means X) or replaced with one everyone knows?

items.label: What they would lose
items.question: Losses weigh about twice as much as gains (Kahneman). Is the cost of not acting shown?

items.label: Costs the teller something
items.question: Is there a piece of you in it: a fact or a story that compels the listener?

items.label: Unforgotten sentence
items.question: Is there one line people will repeat?

items.label: Claims carry receipts
items.question: Does every fact, origin or quote point to its source?

items.label: Open with a concrete number
items.question: Does the paragraph land on one specific number, ratio, or trend that re-frames the topic?

items.label: Quote a comment + engagement
items.question: Is there a comment, quote, or testimony with its engagement count or source attached?

items.label: Cite a study + sample size
items.question: Does a study appear with its sample size, journal, or year so the reader trusts the number?

items.label: Hold a contradiction side-by-side
items.question: Are two opposing facts or quotes placed next to each other so the tension is visible?

items.label: Name a dead predictor
items.question: Does it name someone who predicted this long ago, then grade them against what actually happened?

items.label: Before / after stat with years
items.question: Is there a clear then-vs-now comparison with concrete years and numbers?

items.label: Reframe as pricing / exchange
items.question: Is the argument translated into what someone pays, what they get, and whether the deal still holds?

items.label: The honest version is narrow
items.question: Does it narrow the claim to what the evidence actually supports, instead of overreaching?

items.label: Not-X-but-Y relabeling
items.question: Does the piece swap a word the reader already has for the truer one at least once?

items.label: Not because ___. Because ___.
items.question: Does it kill the default cause and install the real one?

items.label: Numbered engine
items.question: If the piece is long, does it use a counted spine so progress feels inevitable?

items.label: Sentence that turns on itself
items.question: Does the opening betray an expectation in the second half?

items.label: Small fact, enormous implication
items.question: Does the opening give a tiny concrete fact that implies a much larger conclusion?

items.label: Asymmetry
items.question: Does the opening place two numbers side-by-side that should match but don't?

items.label: Declare what you're not doing
items.question: Does it lower the reader's guard by narrowing the battlefield?

items.label: Map the options
items.question: Does it give the reader the whole map early?

items.label: Mechanism not villain
items.question: Does it explain the other side's behavior as a pattern that works for them, not as evil?

items.label: Walk the evidence like a clock
items.question: Does the middle walk evidence slowly and concretely so the conclusion grows out of it?

items.label: Show the other phone
items.question: Does it steel-man the other side's best evidence in their own words?

items.label: Witness with year and book
items.question: Does it bring in a historical thinker with a specific citation and build on one line?

items.label: Hold that in your mind
items.question: Does it load an idea early and fire it later, stitching the argument together?

items.label: Both true at once
items.question: Does it hold a paradox side-by-side without collapsing it?

items.label: Swap test
items.question: Does it use a mirror swap that collapses the opposing verdict?

items.label: The question was never X
items.question: Does it re-ask the question at a deeper level before the close?

items.label: Convict your own side
items.question: Does it concede your own camp's fault first, with data?

items.label: Refused number
items.question: Does it name a claim it will NOT make, and why?

items.label: Compassion to the other side
items.question: Does it show real empathy for the person it is critiquing?

items.label: Aphorism run
items.question: Does the close land with 2-4 short hard sentences people could quote?

items.label: Carry-question
items.question: Does it leave one portable question the reader can keep using?

items.label: Ring to the opening
items.question: Does the close return to the opening's concrete scene or names?

items.label: List then cut
items.question: Does it use a run of concrete nouns ending in one short sentence for rhythm?

outlines.label: Hook → Pain or possibility → Proof → Payoff → Call to action

sections.label: Hook
sections.question: One line that makes the stakes felt.

sections.label: Pain or possibility
sections.question: The specific problem, or the opportunity: why it matters.

sections.label: Proof
sections.question: Data, research, cases: evidence it is real.

sections.label: Payoff
sections.question: Why the reward outweighs the cost, effort or risk; objections answered.

sections.label: Call to action
sections.question: What the reader should do or think now.

sections.label: Context
sections.question: Where and when; who; what was at stake.

sections.label: Action
sections.question: What happened, at the right pace.

sections.label: Takeaway
sections.question: What it means for the reader: why you told it.
